titre: The Cape of Good Hope Is Not Africa's Southern Tip
accroche: Africa's southern tip is Cape Agulhas, 150 km to the east-southeast: since 1953, it is where the boundary between two oceans begins.
contenu_vulgarise:
On many tourist maps, the Cape of Good Hope passes for the southern tip of Africa, where the Atlantic meets the Indian Ocean. The headland is impressive: it borders the Atlantic coast of the Cape Peninsula, about 50 kilometers south of Cape Town. But it lies at about 34° 21' south latitude and 18° 28' east longitude. Cape Agulhas, at 34° 50' south and 20° east, is about half a degree of latitude farther south, some fifty kilometers, and 150 kilometers to the east-southeast.

## The Mechanism

The boundary between the oceans was set in writing. In its Special Publication No. 23, “Limits of Oceans and Seas” (3rd edition, 1953), the International Hydrographic Organization describes the southeastern limit of the South Atlantic as starting from Cape Agulhas and following the 20° east meridian to the Antarctic continent. The western limit of the Indian Ocean is described in the same terms. The boundary is thus a line drawn with a ruler, starting at Cape Agulhas and running due south.

The confusion comes from sailors. Heading down the west coast of Africa from the equator, it is at the Cape of Good Hope that a ship begins to go more east than south. Bartolomeu Dias had named it the Cape of Storms. King John II of Portugal renamed it the Cape of Good Hope, out of optimism at the opening of a sea route to India. The name marks a turn in the route, not the end of a continent.

## The Shift

That leaves the sea, which does not follow the meridian. The warm Agulhas Current runs down Africa's east coast and then, south of Cape Agulhas, doubles back toward the Indian Ocean. As it turns back, it sheds large eddies, the Agulhas rings, which drift into the South Atlantic and carry heat and salt there. The place where this warm current meets the cold Benguela Current oscillates between Cape Agulhas and Cape Point, very close to the Cape of Good Hope.

The Portuguese name of Cape Agulhas, Cabo das Agulhas, means Cape of Needles, and sailors on the clipper route long dreaded its approaches. The 1953 limit is a convention of cartographers, precise and practical. Water from the Indian Ocean crosses it constantly, in eddies.

repere.texte: IHO Special Publication No. 23 (3rd edition, 1953): the limit between the South Atlantic and the Indian Ocean starts at Cape Agulhas and follows the 20° east meridian to the Antarctic continent.
repere.source: International Hydrographic Organization, Limits of Oceans and Seas, S-23, 3rd ed., 1953, Nos. 32 and 45

carte.punch: The Cape of Good Hope is not the southern tip of Africa: Cape Agulhas is.
carte.idee: Cape Agulhas is about 55 km farther south than the Cape of Good Hope. It is from there that the International Hydrographic Organization, in 1953, starts the boundary between the Atlantic and the Indian Ocean: the 20° east meridian, down to Antarctica.
carte.source_courte: IHO, Limits of Oceans and Seas, 1953

quiz.question: Why does the boundary between the Atlantic and the Indian Ocean start at Cape Agulhas?
choix: Because the cold Benguela Current stops exactly at that cape
Because the IHO set the limit by convention on the 20° east meridian, starting from that cape
Because Bartolomeu Dias rounded Africa there and gave it its name
Because the waters there change temperature abruptly along a visible line
quiz.explication: The limit is written in the IHO's 1953 publication: the 20° east meridian starting from Cape Agulhas, the southern tip of Africa. The Benguela Current does not stop there, the meeting of the currents oscillates between that cape and Cape Point, and Dias's name refers to the Cape of Good Hope, formerly the Cape of Storms.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How did the Cape of Good Hope get its name?
choix: Bartolomeu Dias named it that in honor of King John II
King John II renamed it out of optimism, after the Cape of Storms given by Dias
IHO cartographers renamed it in 1953 to simplify the boundary of the oceans
The name comes from the warm current that brings there, according to sailors, the hope of a calm sea
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Bartolomeu Dias had called this cape the Cape of Storms, and King John II renamed it out of optimism at the opening of a route to India, not for any oceanographic or cartographic reason.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What becomes of the Agulhas rings, shed by the retroflection of the warm current south of Cape Agulhas?
choix: They drift into the South Atlantic and carry heat and salt there
They travel up Africa's east coast to the equator
They dissolve immediately on contact with the cold Benguela Current
They follow the 20° east meridian set by the IHO in 1953
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Agulhas Current doubles back toward the Indian Ocean south of the cape, and the eddies it sheds drift into the South Atlantic, bringing heat and salt there, without traveling up toward the equator, dissolving on contact with the Benguela Current, or following a meridian.
